text:
Vasily Podkolzin is the breakout of Edmonton's season. At 25 he plays 17:58 a night, up from 15:23 last season, and he is on the ice for 47% of the Oilers' power-play chances (12% a year ago). He has 13 goals and 22 points in 26 games, 0.85 a game after 0.45 last season, with 80 hits and a five-game point streak.

The role change is real. His own chances are up to 1.17 expected goals per 60 from 0.78 (expected goals measure chance quality), and at 5v5 the Oilers take 60.4% of the attempts with him on the ice. Our wins-added measure has him 21st in the league.

The finishing is the part to discount. He has 13 goals on 9.1 expected, shooting 25% against 14% last season, and Edmonton has scored 11.8 more goals than expected with him out there. Our talent range has his shooting closer to 15.1%.

His minutes have climbed lately too: 20.7, 21.8 and 24.7 in the last three games, all without an Oilers win. The chances, not the 25% shooting, are what keep a player in a role like this.
